# AES-128-GCM test cases, frozen. One case per line:
#   <source> <verdict> <key> <iv> <aad> <msg> <ct> <tag>
# with '-' for an empty field. Every case is a 128-bit key, a 96-bit IV and
# a 128-bit tag, which is the only shape this module implements -- TLS uses
# no other, and a wider net would mean writing code no caller can reach.
#
# Two sources, and they answer different questions.
#
#  is Google's adversarial corpus (testvectors_v1,
# aes_gcm_test.json), filtered to that shape: the cases carry their own
# verdict, and the invalid ones are what a lenient implementation accepts --
# a tag of the wrong length, a flipped bit, a counter that wrapped.
#
#  is a length sweep generated once against OpenSSL 3.6.3 and
# frozen: every combination of twenty-one payload and AAD lengths chosen to
# sit on and around each block boundary (0, 15, 16, 17, 31, ... 257, 300).
# That is where a carry-less multiply's tail handling and a CTR mode's
# partial final block go wrong, and a wrong answer there is invisible to the
# round-trip test that would otherwise cover it -- both directions would
# agree with each other and with nothing else.
